## d2534264df36

**Classification: generator-domain question / surviving shortcut, not a reproduced in-domain correctness bug; target left unchanged.** Generator SHA-256 `54b8db08296bc4df54eabc45e73adee45809bb57386b76f6d2cdc49c426e43ca`.

Every generated side role uses two same-color inward witnesses. A `paired_only` rival that fills a ring side only after seeing such a pair matched the task's Python authority mirror on 1,050/1,050 generated inputs: all seven profiles, all three bands, 50 draws per profile-band cell. Thus generated lessons cannot distinguish “each non-corner source acts independently” from “a matched pair activates the side role.” Evidence: `checks/audit/d2534264df36/probe.json` and retained rival output `checks/audit/d2534264df36/paired_only_rival.json`.

A 19×19 counterexample with one corner source and only one non-corner source on the same ring is executable under the canonical authority. Racket propagates the lone side witness around all four sides, while the paired-only rival does not. The current `self_check` rejects this input with `arm_pair`, `no_side_role`, `ring_chain`, `unaccounted_sources`, and `unsupported_profile`, so this is explicitly outside the documented training grammar. It should be treated as a coverage/induction decision, not evidence that approved generated inputs are mislabeled. Input: `checks/audit/d2534264df36/input.json`; Racket result: `checks/audit/d2534264df36/racket.json`.

Racket command, packet-root cwd: `python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply d2534264df36 --input ../checks/audit/d2534264df36/input.json --out ../checks/audit/d2534264df36/racket.json` (exit 0). A possible false positive is intentional restriction to the paired public morphology; no fix was made.
